faq.a: Because chess is a motor-spatial reflex skill, not a lecture. When you watch video, you engage passive auditory memory. When you touch the board and make interactive decisions with immediate feedback, your brain forms spatial muscle memory 5x faster.

CCT is the structured mental discipline used by strong players before every move: 1) Checks against the enemy king, 2) Captures of hanging or loose pieces, 3) Threats of forks, pins, and skewers. Systematizing CCT stops 80% of tactical blunders before they happen.

At ratings below 1600 Elo, 85%+ of games are determined by tactical blunders, not master-level opening nuances. Memorizing 25 moves of the Catalan is useless when your opponent deviates on move 3. CCT and tactical survival work in every single position.

faq.q: Is this suitable if I'm stuck at a 1000–1400 Elo plateau?
faq.a: That is the exact sweet spot. Adult improvers in the 1000–1400 bracket almost always plateau due to tactical blindness and unforced blunders. BlunderProof was engineered precisely to shatter this plateau.
